name: Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport
before:
Bangladesh's largest airport and the main gateway to Dhaka, at Kurmitola 17 km from the city centre in the northern part of the city.

Capacity is the pressure point. The airport is rated for 18.5 million passengers a year, and the civil aviation authority predicted that would be sufficient only until 2026, so it is at or approaching its ceiling. It handles around 190 aircraft movements a day.

The code is a relic worth knowing. DAC comes from Dacca, the older spelling of Dhaka, so it does not match the airport's name or the city's current spelling.

It is the primary hub for most Bangladeshi airlines including the flag carrier Biman Bangladesh, plus Air Astra, Novoair and US-Bangla.

It opened in 1980, taking over from Tejgaon Airport, and was formerly called Dacca International and then Zia International before being named after Shah Jalal, one of the most respected Sufi saints in Bangladesh. It also hosts a Bangladesh Air Force base.
after:
Dhaka's airport and the largest in Bangladesh, at Kurmitola about 17 km from the city centre in the northern part of the city.

Capacity is the pressure point. The terminals were designed for 8 million passengers a year but handled about 12.7 million in 2025. A third terminal is due for a soft opening on 16 December 2026, the government says, so check which terminal a client will use.

Biman Bangladesh, the flag carrier, is based here, as are US-Bangla, Novoair and Air Astra.

It took over from Tejgaon Airport and was first called Dacca International, then Zia International, before being named after the Sufi saint Shah Jalal.

The airport is well past its design capacity: TBS (19 July 2026) gives 1.27 crore (12.7 million) travellers in 2025, up from 1.25 crore in 2024; Wikipedia's infobox gives 12,720,000 for 2025, citing CAAB. The passenger total corrects the old text's claim about how close the airport is to capacity; it is not a figure added where the old text had none.

claims.claim: a third terminal is due for a soft opening on 16 December 2026, the government says
claims.inAfter: A third terminal is due for a soft opening on 16 December 2026, the government says
claims.note: Replaces the forecast that capacity would last 'only until 2026' (cut below): the capacity outlook now is the third terminal, which the minister says will double passenger capacity (The Daily Star, 30 August 2026). The minister told reporters the government is working to hold a soft opening on 16 December (The Daily Star, 24 August 2026); TBS (17 September 2026) says CAAB plans to begin partial operations by 16 December; TBS (19 July 2026) and Wikipedia (a statement of April 2026) give 16 December or early 2027. It is given as the government's plan: the terminal has stood idle for about 19 months over the operating deal with a Japanese consortium (TBS, 28 July 2026), and on 30 August the minister said it still needed Tk 902 crore to clear dues and finish works (The Daily Star). The advice to check the terminal is listed under opinion.

claims.claim: Held back: FCDO advice on Dhaka airport (theft, harassment, taxi overcharging; frequent short-notice disruption to air travel)
claims.why: Held back: a warning that replaces nothing in the old text. The FCDO's Bangladesh advice (updated 4 September 2026, still current 24 September) says Dhaka's international airport is fully operational; lists theft (including passport theft), harassment and overcharging of taxi fees as risks there, and advises avoiding touts, keeping documents safe and arranging taxis in advance; and warns of frequent disruptions to air travel, often at short notice, and slow airport security checks.
